raw_response:
I have been farming cotton here in Quzhou for 42 years, so I know this land well. With 15 mu, I have some room to manage properly but I still watch every yuan. Let me think through this season.

For my seed, I will stick with Bt hybrid cotton — I have used it for years and it handles bollworm much better than the old varieties. The seed costs more but I save on pesticide sprays and my neighbors who still plant traditional seed spray twice as often as me. I will plant around late April when soil temperature is steady above 14 degrees.

For fertilizer, my soil here is loam-clay, pH slightly alkaline like most Quzhou land. Cotton is a long-season crop and pulls a lot of nitrogen, but too much nitrogen makes it grow tall and leafy with fewer bolls — I learned that the hard way back in the 1990s. I will apply about 18 kg of pure nitrogen per mu, split: one-third as base before planting with the compound fertilizer, and two-thirds as topdressing at squaring and flowering. For phosphorus I use about 10 kg per mu as base — cotton needs phosphorus early for root development. Potassium I push a bit harder than most neighbors, about 12 kg per mu, because potassium gives me better boll weight and fiber quality, and our soil tests low. I usually buy a 15-15-15 compound for base and urea plus potassium sulfate for topdressing.

Irrigation: I have well access, so I will water 4 times — once before planting to ensure emergence, once at squaring, once at peak flowering, and once at boll-filling. I skip late irrigation so bolls open cleanly.

Pesticide: even with Bt, I still have to deal with aphids, spider mites, and plant bugs. I plan 6 sprays across the season, combining insecticide with a growth regulator (mepiquat chloride) to control plant height.

I will plough the field deeply this year since I did rotary last year — deep ploughing every 2-3 years breaks up the hardpan and helps roots go deeper.

Expected yield: if weather cooperates, 280 kg seed cotton per mu is realistic. My best year was 320, but I plan conservatively.
